title: review: E2: Jev client — orchestrator/jev.py typed questions against TypeSafe AI System One, fail-open, budgeted
spec:
Jev (TypeSafe AI) answers typed questions about a state with calibrated probabilities instead of text: POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone, header Authorization: Bearer <key>, body {"state": str|obj, "model": "jev-latest", "questions": {id: {"type": "noul"|"choice"|"score", "instructions": str, "criteria": ...}}}; response {"answers": {id: {"type", "noul": 0-1, "choice": str, "probabilities": {opt: p}, "score": n, "confidence": 0-1}}, "usage": {"input_tokens", "output_tokens"}}. Limits: 64k tokens per request, 32k for state + longest question; 429/529 need backoff; 0.042 USD per M input tokens, output free. New module orchestrator/jev.py, stdlib only (urllib):
1. ask(state, questions, *, model=None, timeout_s=5.0) -> dict | None. Reads pool.toml [jev] {enabled=false, model="jev-latest", timeout_s=5, daily_budget_tokens=20_000_000, max_state_chars=100_000} and the key from env TYPESAFE_API_KEY (pool.toml [secrets.jev] TYPESAFE_API_KEY = "source ~/.config/f/f.sh && f tok get typesafe --reveal" on the laptop, env:TYPESAFE_API_KEY headless; resolved through spawn.resolve_secrets, never logged). Returns None (fail-open) when disabled, no key, timeout, HTTP error, invalid JSON or budget exhausted; one retry with 0.5 s backoff on 429/529.
2. State hygiene before sending: truncate to max_state_chars, redact anything matching token-like patterns (sk-..., ghp_..., Bearer ..., 32+ char hex/base64 runs, KEY=VALUE where KEY contains TOKEN|SECRET|PASSWORD|KEY). Provide redact(text) as a tested public helper.
3. Usage accounting: append {ts, caller, input_tokens, model, latency_ms, ok} to .orchestrator/runs/jev-<date>.jsonl and keep the day counter in .orchestrator/jev_state.json; ask() returns None when the day counter exceeds daily_budget_tokens.
4. Helpers: noul(state, instructions, criteria=None) -> float | None (P(true)); choice(state, instructions, options: dict) -> (choice, probabilities, confidence) | None; score(state, instructions, levels: list) -> (score, confidence) | None.
Tests in tests/test_jev.py with a monkeypatched urlopen: disabled returns None without network; happy path parses answers; 429 retried once then None; redact() strips a fake token; budget exhaustion returns None; oversize state is truncated. README: one paragraph 'Jev' under Pipeline with the egress note (task specs, tool-call metadata and memory titles leave the machine; file contents never do).
acceptance: pool.toml has a commented [jev] table with enabled = false and [secrets.jev] with the two documented value forms; no secret value in any file

comments.issue: Dead config: `[jev].timeout_s` is read into `_cfg()["timeout_s"]` (line 56) but never used. `ask()` hardcodes the keyword default `timeout_s=5.0` and passes that to `urlopen` (line 125), so setting `timeout_s = 30` in pool.toml — a knob the commented table at pool.toml:185 advertises — has no effect. Same class as the T-0212 fix round (TOOLS[role] defined but never reaching argv). Fix: `timeout_s = timeout_s if timeout_s is not None else cfg["timeout_s"]` with the signature default set to None.

`_log_usage` writes `jev-<date>.jsonl` into `.orchestrator/runs/`, the same directory `bus.log_run` writes worker runs to, and two consumers glob it indiscriminately: `cli.cost()` (cli.py:20) sums `input_tokens` over every `*.jsonl` line keyed by `e.get(by, "?")`, so jev calls inflate a bogus `?` row and the `runs` count in `orchestrator cost`; `scorecard.build(by="tier")` (scorecard.py:76,81) likewise creates a `?` executor row from jev entries. The test's own tearDown comment concedes the collision (it has to delete jev files so test_spawn's `sorted(glob("*.jsonl"))[-1]` stays correct) — production has no such cleanup. Write to a separate dir (e.g. `STATE / "jev_runs"`) or give entries a discriminator both consumers filter on.

Budget check uses `>` instead of `>=`, so a call is admitted when the tally already equals the budget, and `daily_budget_tokens = 0` — the obvious way to hard-stop spend without editing `enabled` — never blocks anything: `_day_tokens_used()` starts at 0, `0 > 0` is false, so the first call always goes out (and every subsequent one until the tally exceeds 0). Should be `>=`.

`_add_day_tokens` is an unlocked read-modify-write (`_load_state()` then `write_text`), unlike the repo's own convention for the same pattern in `pool._save_planner_account`, which takes an flock on the file precisely so a concurrent tally can't clobber an entry. Two daemon processes calling jev concurrently lose counts; a crash mid-`write_text` truncates the file, and `_load_state`'s JSONDecodeError fallback then silently resets the day's tally to 0 — the budget under-counts in exactly the case it exists to guard.

`_api_key()` runs on every `ask()` and goes through `spawn.secrets_for_role`, which constructs a full `Pool()` (re-reads pool.toml and pool_state.json, already read once by `_cfg()` in the same call) and then `subprocess.run(['bash','-c', 'source ~/.config/f/f.sh && f tok get ...'])` — a Keychain-backed shell per question. For a client whose whole point is cheap 5s typed questions (`noul`/`choice`/`score` are one call each), that is a large fixed overhead per call and is unbounded if a caller loops. Cache the resolved key for the process lifetime.

No test covers the README's central safety claim that `ask()` redacts before anything leaves the machine. `test_redact_strips_tokens` exercises `redact()` in isolation and `test_state_truncated` asserts the captured payload equals `long_state[:50]` verbatim (token-free input), so removing the `redact(...)` wrapper at jev.py:118 leaves the whole suite green. Worth a capture-based test asserting a `sk-` token in `state` never appears in `req.data`. Related: `redact` is applied after truncation, so a secret straddling `max_state_chars` is cut below the `{10,}`/`{32,}` thresholds and ships unredacted.
